text_blocks.snippet: EGFR-positive lung cancer refers to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with a mutation in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene. This mutation causes the EGFR protein to become overactive, promoting cancer cell growth and spread. Targeted therapy drugs, like tyrosine kinase inhibitors, are often used to treat EGFR-positive NSCLC, offering a more personalized approach than traditional chemotherapy, according to Verywell Health.
